decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - 1.	The proposed side and rear roof extensions, incorporating a hipped roof to gable end conversion, by reason of its disproportionate bulk and the unbalancing effect it would have on this pair of semi-detached houses would represent an obtrusive development, detrimental to the appearance of the original property and street scene, contrary to UDP policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development) and H.6.4 (Extensions and Alterations) of the Adopted Unitary Development Plan and Section 5.0 (Roof extensions, Roof lights & Solar Panels, Roof terraces & Balconies) of the Residential Extension Guidelines.

Condition : 2 - The local planning authority cannot consider the proposed rear loft extension in the absence of the hip to gable conversion which has yet to be built and in isolation from it at this stage.

Once the applicant is able to demonstrate that the hip to gable extension, which has been granted a certificate of lawfulness, has been substantially completed (and not before that time), a planning application for the rear loft extension alone can then be considered on its own merits.
description: Erection of side and rear roof extensions to house, incorporating conversion of hip end to gable end roof.
